interactions.summary: Jiang turns student answers about ancestry into a fuller model: remembered deeds, family destiny, ancestral authority, and unfinished inheritance combine to reassure Dante and strip away ego and fear.
Jiang closes before the break by explaining Dante's chronology: the poem is written in 1321 but set in 1300 so the ancestor's prophecy can forecast the 1302 exile from within the story.

claims.claim: Jiang says Dante's lasting inheritance is not wealth or worldly achievement but remembered action, which is what survives into family memory.
He says family history reassures Dante because it suggests a plan already in motion: ancestors enacted their part, Dante has arrived at his appointed point, and he must now do his part.
Jiang endorses the student view that ancestral authority matters because ancestors are trusted as wiser figures who can reassure Dante more effectively than his own judgment can.
Jiang says inherited achievement is not just consolation but unfinished obligation: Dante must add his own contribution to the family line even if he gains no fame in life.
He says that seeing himself as part of a family legacy cleanses Dante by removing ego and fear before the prophecy scene.

Jiang dates the composition frame by saying Dante finished the Divine Comedy in 1321, set the story in 1300, and uses the ancestor's speech to forecast the 1302 exile from inside that earlier narrative moment.
claims.temporal_scope: Chronology explanation stated on 2026-06-17 about years 1300, 1302, and 1321.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang reduces legacy to a hard remainder: wealth vanishes, achievement fades, but remembered action is what the world keeps.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Not your wealth, not your achievements, but your actions
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the packet its sharpest criterion for what survives exile and death.

signature_moments.moment: Family lineage becomes destiny machinery: Dante did not randomly arrive at crisis, he has reached the point prepared for him from the beginning.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there is a plan in motion
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's cleanest local statement that genealogy is not nostalgia but providential structure.

signature_moments.moment: The burden of lineage acts like spiritual detergent: belonging to a family line removes the ego and fear that would otherwise deform Dante's mission.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's removing the ego and fear from him
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the packet's most reusable psychological mechanism for why ancestry matters in this canto.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes Dante's prophecy legible by folding time: the 1321 poet stages a 1300 self so an ancestor can announce the 1302 wound as future.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he set his character in the year 1300, so that his grandfather can tell him what will happen in the year 1302
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures the temporal architecture that underwrites Jiang's reading of Canto 17.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's phrase for family history as evidence that Dante's suffering and vocation belong to a providential design.
The lineage Dante must add to, which for Jiang becomes the instrument that strips ego and fear away.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 Jiang moves from the psychological use of ancestry into a precise timeline: author Dante writes with hindsight in 1321, story Dante stands in 1300, and the coming 1302 exile is staged as prophecy.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR phrase "you have to find comedy" is almost certainly a mishearing in context; the safe semantic takeaway is that Dante must complete his contribution to the family legacy through the Comedy.
